## Setup

This is the SSH chain: $2n$ sites with alternating weak bonds $t_1$ (within unit cells) and strong bonds $t_2$ (between cells), in the topological phase ($t_2>t_1$). The bulk spectrum has bands $\pm\varepsilon(k)$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\sqrt{t_1^2+t_2^2+2t_1t_2\cos k}$, but the lowest excitation comes from the two exponentially localized edge modes, which hybridize through the chain.

## Zero-mode splitting

Zero-energy states live only on odd sites (amplitudes $x_{2j-1}$, decay constant $t_1/t_2$):
$$t_1 x_{2j-1}+t_2 x_{2j+1}=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \cosh\!\big((2j-1)\eta\big)=A\cosh\theta+B\sinh\theta,\qquad e^\eta=t_2/t_1,$$
where $\theta=(2j-1)\eta-\ln[2A/(A+B)]$. The open boundary conditions require $A=B$ at the left end and $A=-B$ at the right end, which at energy $\varepsilon$ become $\tanh\theta=\pm\tanh(\varepsilon/t_2)$. The quantization condition is therefore
$$\tanh(n\eta)=\tanh(\varepsilon/t_1).$$
For small $\varepsilon$, setting $\tanh\theta=\pm\varepsilon/t_2$ and using $\tanh(n\eta-\theta)=\tanh(n\eta-\theta+2\theta)$ to extract the linear term gives
$$\varepsilon_1=\frac{t_2^2-t_1^2}{t_2}\tanh(n\eta)\;\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}\;\frac{t_2^2-t_1^2}{t_2}\left(\frac{t_1}{t_2}\right)^{n}.$$

Particle–hole symmetry pairs the levels as $\pm\varepsilon_k$, so the hybridized edge levels are $\pm\varepsilon_1$.
